extraction.title: Free Exchange
extraction.subtitle: The myth of the petrodollar The dominance of America's currency runs deeper than oil
extraction.summary: The article traces the origin of the "petrodollar" concept, its role in cementing US dollar dominance through oil pricing and secret Treasury bond purchases, and examines how recent geopolitical shifts—especially the Iran war and China's push for yuan‑based oil payments—are challenging that regime, while also introducing the broader idea of "hostage capital" as a risk to the dollar's future.

events.event_summary: Ibrahim Oweiss coins term "petrodollar" in a speech.
US Treasury allows Saudi central bank to buy Treasury bonds secretly.
Saudi Aramco adopts dollar‑only pricing for crude exports.
Saudi Arabia runs current‑account deficits, reducing petrodollar inflows.
Combined oil‑exporter surplus falls to $200bn, far below East Asian manufacturers' surplus.
Iran war intensifies scrutiny of petrodollar regime; China, Russia, India explore non‑dollar oil payments.

themes.name: Petrodollar dominance

themes.name: Hostage capital
themes.description: US financial sanctions and asset seizure as systemic risk.

narratives.name: Petrodollar as pillar of US dollar dominance
narratives.thesis: The concentration of oil revenues in dollars since the 1970s has underpinned the United States' financial and geopolitical power.

narratives.name: Erosion of petrodollar dominance
narratives.thesis: Geopolitical conflicts and the rise of alternative currencies (yuan, digital yuan) are gradually weakening the dollar's monopoly over oil trade.

narratives.name: Hostage capital concept
narratives.thesis: US ability to freeze or confiscate foreign assets creates systemic risk that may drive countries away from the dollar, beyond the petrodollar mechanism.
